content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate candy are small sweets made from chocolate (milk, dark or white) with a variety of fillings such as nuts, caramel, fruit, spices, and more. They have a rich cocoa flavor, aromatic notes, and are often coated with glaze or sprinkles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first chocolate bar was created in 1847 in England.
Chocolate candies are popular gifts for holidays like Valentine’s Day, Easter, and Christmas.
Dark chocolate contains over 70% cocoa and is considered healthier than milk chocolate.
In some countries (e.g., Switzerland) per‑capita consumption exceeds 10 kg per year.
Chocolate candies can be gluten‑free, but always check the filling ingredients.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Dark chocolate is high in flavonoids, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: Chocolate stimulates serotonin and endorphin production, improving mood.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Chocolate provides magnesium, iron, zinc, and copper, important for metabolism.

items.title: Contains some fiber
items.content: When nuts or dried fruit are included, they add dietary fiber.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: Sugar and fat deliver fast energy, useful during periods of high activity.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive intake can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Candies often contain nuts, milk, soy lecithin – common allergens.

items.title: Caffeine and theobromine
items.content: Large amounts may cause insomnia or rapid heartbeat, especially in children.

items.title: Trans fats in some varieties
items.content: Certain industrial candies use hydrogenated fats, which are harmful to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Candies can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to baked goods, ice cream, or dessert sauces. For a softer taste, they are sometimes gently warmed to melt the chocolate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep candies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Above 20 °C the chocolate may melt, and high humidity can cause a white bloom (fat bloom).
